newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov sees trade with China increasing.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov sees trade with China increasing.

text.p: Top Russian reformer Boris Nemtsov said on Saturday he aimed to boost languishing trade ties with China on a visit next week and that Moscow expects to win a tender to supply equipment for a major Chinese project.

Nemtsov, one of two first deputy prime ministers and one of Russia's most popular politicians, told a news conference that China's investment in Russia's nascent market economy was "laughably low" at $120 million.
Russian news agencies quoted Nemtsov, who leaves for China on Monday, as lamenting the relatively meagre level of trade between the two giant neighbours.
"Nemtsov said the annual trade turnover between Russia and China, which stands at $6.8 billion, is extremely insignificant and must be increased," Interfax news agency reported.
Nemtsov said Moscow had submitted a tender for $10 billion worth of equipment for China's huge "Three Gorges" hydro-electrical project on the Yangtse river.
Moscow faced stiff competition from France, the United States and Canada but expected to win, Interfax quoted him as saying.

Russia was preparing to sign seven documents on boosting trade ties, Itar-Tass news agency said. These included agreements on oil projects such as one to develop oil and gas deposits in Russia's remote Irkutsk region and another on building pipelines to South Korea.
No further details were available on the projects.

Russia and China share a 4,000 km (2,500 mile) border and have seen their political and economic relations rise and fall over the years. Those ties received a considerable boost in April when Chinese President Jiang Zemin visited Moscow.

Both countries hailed the visit as the start of a new era. Nemtsov's visit, to prepare for Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's own trip to Beijing later this month, is intended to add substance to the presidents' political declarations.
